item.title: ExRel: Learning Directed Reuse Relevance between Rich-Text K-12 Question Images with Executable Relation Contracts
item.description: In K-12 education, question images combine text, mathematical expressions, diagrams, and diverse layouts. Variations in wording, conditions, answer options, or task scope can substantially alter their reuse utility despite visual similarity. We formulate this problem as directed reuse relevance, grading candidate utility as Strong, Medium, or Weak. However, generic similarity scores overlook task-specific reuse requirements, while natural supervision is dominated by Strong relations and lacks fi...

item.title: How did data sharing evolve in the decade since the FAIR Principles?
item.description: A decade after the publication of the FAIR Guiding Principles, what have we learned about data sharing, and what do data availability statements (DAS) and other materials accrued over that period tell us about how data-sharing practices, attitudes, and infrastructures evolved? Here, we present a large-scale longitudinal analysis of over 6.8 million biomedical articles from the PMC Open Access Subset, spanning 2011 to 2025. Using an automated pipeline, we extracted and classified DAS, repository ...

item.title: TokenFormer V2: Breaking the Resolution-Complexity Dilemma in Unified Recommendation
item.description: Industrial recommendation faces a resolution--complexity dilemma: dense interactions make detailed modeling of long behavior histories expensive, while compact history summaries restrict the evidence available to prediction. A unified backbone must preserve rich behavioral details within strict serving budgets. We introduce \textbf{TokenFormer V2}, a unified architecture that explicitly decouples \emph{representation resolution} from \emph{interaction density}. Its group-wise token layout jointl...

item.title: Living Context Graphs: Continual Semantic Learning for Enterprise Data Reasoning
item.description: Enterprise AI can now perform analytics, reporting, and data-driven workflows, yet the data foundations it relies on remain hard to operationalize: business meaning, relationships, metric definitions, and reporting conventions are absent from database schemas and scattered across undocumented systems and tribal knowledge. We introduce the Living Context Graph (LCG), a continually learned context layer that makes existing enterprise data operational for AI without requiring a copy or transformati...

item.title: Evidence Diet: When Graph Evidence Helps LLMs Rank Competing Candidates
item.description: When several candidates have graph support, does it matter which candidate receives which supporter and path counts? We study how LLM rankers use collaborative evidence on Amazon Books and MovieTV. Swapping user-level evidence degrades ranking, while matched item substitutions have little effect. On fixed clean-trained checkpoints, unrelated catalog text lowers Hit@1 from 44.77% to 38.70%, with 99.9% of rankings still valid. Across all three paired seeds, the NDCG@5 difference between count and ...

item.title: When the Bill Falls: Reusing the Old Index Defers,Never Avoids, Re-encoding in Complete Embedding-Model Migration
item.description: Upgrading the embedding model behind a vector index requires re-encoding the corpus. Recent work reuses the old index through adapters or window re-ranking. Across sixteen model pairs on passage and code corpora, plus eleven on Natural Questions (NQ), we find three results. First, reuse never avoids re-encoding: if migration must complete, every strategy eventually encodes every document; reuse only changes when that work is paid and the quality served meanwhile. Second, adapters should be compa...

item.title: Leveraging Binary Hashing for Scalable Index Assignment in Semantic Communications
item.description: Transmitting semantically structured embedding vectors over digital channels is costly in bit rate, while conven- tional vector quantization approaches face limitations in scalabil- ity, encoding complexity, and index assignment. This paper inves- tigates binary hashing techniques from the information retrieval literature as semantic indexing strategies for general-purpose networks. We study random Locality-Sensitive Hashing (LSH) along with Principal Component Analysis (PCA)-, Canonical Correla...

item.title: EE-Motion: An EEG-based Web Architecture for Live Affective Music Recommendation
item.description: Music listening is intrinsically tied to emotion, which drifts continuously within a single session. Although modern browsers interface with wearable brain-computer interfaces, recommendation systems remain structured around discrete logs and lack the infrastructure to integrate continuous physiological signals. Furthermore, existing affect-aware models rely on static user profiles and offline training, failing to serve anonymous newcomers without model retraining. We present a web platform that...

item.title: Adaptive-Elbow Graph Traversal for Schema Retrieval in Text-to-SQL
item.description: LLM-based natural-language interfaces to relational databases are gated by a schema-retrieval step: the generator can only be as good as the slice of schema it is shown. On a database with hundreds of tables, that slice must be selected and the selection is two-sided---omit a needed table and the query becomes unrecoverable, include too many and the irrelevant ones act as noise that degrades the model's output. When an agentic retriever that lets the model inspect the schema can be too costly or...

item.title: MAGE: Meta-path Adaptive Graph Evidence for Transferable Multimodal Graph Learning
item.description: Multimodal graphs integrate textual and visual attributes with relational structures, providing a rich representation of complex real-world data. To enable the broad applicability and reuse of graph models, it is crucial for models trained on source graphs to generalize to unseen graph domains. However, this is challenging because cross-modal interactions among neighbors and the neighboring information needed for prediction can vary across target nodes and graph domains. This gives rise to two k...

item.title: UniGraph: A Unified Graph-based Index for Dynamic Hybrid Dense-Sparse Vector Retrieval
item.description: Hybrid dense-sparse vector retrieval combines semantic signals from dense representations with lexical signals from sparse representations, typically ranking items by a query-dependent weighted sum of dense and sparse vector distances. Existing systems commonly search separate dense and sparse vector indexes and rerank the union of their candidates, incurring two retrieval passes and potentially discarding items that rank highly only after the semantic and lexical signals are combined. Construct...

item.title: CARE: Contrastive-Anchored Residual Encoding with Listwise Reconstruction for Retrieval-Oriented Semantic IDs
item.description: Generative retrieval replaces nearest-neighbor search with the generation of a document's semantic ID (SID), so the SID tokenizer bounds what the retriever can recall. Common SID constructions (residual k-means, RQ-VAE, finite scalar quantization, capacity balancing) optimize criteria defined on document embeddings alone and do not control whether a query can still find its relevant documents after quantization. We propose two retrieval-oriented SID tokenizers. CARE-SID (Contrastive-Anchored Res...

item.title: IntentFlow: An Intent-Driven Real-Time Multimodal Search System with Image-Text Queries at Xiaohongshu
item.description: Multimodal search with image-text queries helps users find notes in user-generated content (UGC) communities and serves as a key search tool for multimodal search agents. For such queries, query-note relevance depends on the user's retrieval intent and cannot be determined by visual or topical similarity alone. Simply reranking visual search results cannot fully address this challenge, as notes relevant to the user's intent may be missing from the initial candidate set. This motivates explicit i...

item.title: Overview of the Plagiarism Detection Task at PAN 2026
item.description: The generative plagiarism detection task at PAN 2026 aims at retrieving the original scientific sources for given automatically generated textual plagiarism. We created two novel datasets of synthetically generated plagiarism following the premise of a malicious actor trying to generate papers with minimal effort while evading detection of undisclosed re-use. We utilized four widely available LLMs: GPT-OSS 120B, Llama 3.1 8B, Qwen 3.5 27B FP8, and DeepSeek-R1 Distill Llama 8B. In this task overv...

item.title: What Unlinked Aggregates Still Prove: Ranker Comparisons from Exact and Differentially Private Item Counts
item.description: Privacy controls can prevent an evaluator from linking purchases to the recommendations users received, while a merchant can still release complete item-level purchase counts for the evaluation cohort. We ask when these counts identify which recommender performs better. The counts constrain who could have bought each item. We bound the performance difference over all assignments consistent with the counts. A reduced transportation network handles full catalogs and can certify attainable endpoint...

item.title: Straight to the Product: What Online Retailers Miss When Shoppers Ask AI First
item.description: When people ask an AI assistant what to buy, what happens next at the store? We link the same people's assistant conversations to their later browsing at twenty large online retailers. People go to the product the assistant named: among shoppers who had not visited the store in the past week, visits to the named product within a day rise from 0.02 to 2.07 per 100 answers (+2.0 points [1.7, 2.4]), and on days with a product-page visit at the store, 44% show a product from their own answer, agains...

item.title: Attribute or Abstain: Evaluating Evidence-Grounded Retrieval on the Low-Resource African Business Web
item.description: Retrieval-augmented systems that research companies are judged by how much they find, yet in markets where public evidence is sparse, a confident answer without support costs more than no answer. We introduce AfriBizClaims, a benchmark of 150 company-research queries across six African markets in English, French and Portuguese, including queries about fictitious companies that a correct system must decline. Each claim a system makes is judged against the page it cites by an AI judge, checked aga...

item.title: NoLBERT-Calls: Reading Earnings Calls Without Hindsight
item.description: Language models are now a standard tool for measuring what managers say on earnings calls, but the encoders behind these measures were usually pretrained on text from the same years a backtest covers. Holding out a test period does not remove that hindsight, because it sits in the features. We adapt NoLBERT, an encoder pretrained only on text published between 1976 and 1995, to earnings calls without letting it read anything dated after 31 December 2023. The calls supply the training signal them...

item.title: Exact Sparse Assignment with Costly Target Embeddings: Fixed-Realization Certificates and an Empirical Audit
item.description: Embedding-based one-to-one association is common in vision and data integration: detections are associated with tracks and records are linked across databases. Such pipelines often solve a sparse optional assignment whose edge scores add a cheap term to an inner product of neural embeddings. When target embeddings are costly, one can acquire them selectively and stop once a certificate proves that the current assignment is optimal. We give such a certificate for unit-norm embeddings. It bounds t...

item.title: StaleBench: Isolating Stale Retrieval in Agent Memory, and Pricing the Fix
item.description: An agent that stores facts over time eventually stores several versions of the same fact. Asked a value-agnostic question - "which team does X play for now?" - a similarity retriever cannot prefer the current version, because every version matches the entity the query names. StaleBench isolates this stale-retrieval failure on 892 real updating facts, with currency labels from the source (Wikidata validity years via TempLAMA), never from a retrieval score. Our central result is that retrieval met...

item.title: EchoSpec: Training Search Agents to Weigh Evidence Above Echoes
item.description: Search agents trained with reinforcement learning decide what to retrieve, when to search again, and when to answer. In real corpora, one claim is copied and paraphrased across many pages while the primary source settling a question appears once. We show that reinforcement-learned search agents grant echoes the credence of independent sources and lose their ability to abstain. Across five base models from 3B to 32B and seven released RL agents on multi-hop Wikipedia questions with primary eviden...

item.title: Take a Step Back: A Dual-Granularity Raw Feature Empowered Intermediate Fusion Graph Convolutional Network for Multimodal Recommendation
item.description: Although multimodal recommendations have shown the ability to learn user preferences and item properties by leveraging explicit multimodal information, they remain constrained by two critical limitations: low-quality representation learning and modality fusion. For the former, existing solutions primarily focus on multi-granularity representation learning; however, we argue that training such representations is difficult due to the inherent data sparsity problem in recommendation scenarios. For ...

item.title: DetouR: Plugging Association Routes into Search Agents for Multi-hop Question Answering
item.description: Search agents answer multi-hop questions by interleaving reasoning with retrieval, deciding at each step what to search next. Existing agents follow semantic routes: they infer what is missing and phrase it as a query, reaching only what the model can name. Yet the decisive page is often one the question never names, frequently just one hyperlink away from evidence already retrieved. Following such association routes reaches more gold pages than semantic search under the same budget. Exploiting ...

item.title: Revisiting What Makes a Good Context Subset: A Sparse Latent Basis Perspective
item.description: Selecting context subsets is increasingly important in modern LLM inference, yet what makes a subset effective remains unclear. We study this question in the controlled setting of few-shot demonstration selection. We examine a hypothesis that demonstrations should collectively provide task-relevant information needed by a target query. Assuming that the query representation provides a useful proxy for these requirements, we formulate selection as sparse reconstruction and instantiate it with Res...

item.title: A Demonstration System for Faithful Temporal Question Answering
item.description: Temporal question answering (TQA) aims to answer questions that involve temporal constraints or require temporal information. We propose Faith, a novel TQA approach that operates over heterogeneous sources and ensures explainable answers by presenting traceable and faithful evidence. In Faith, we design a new recursive answering mechanism transforming implicit temporal constraints into explicit conditions. Additionally, we visualize the system functionality to track how the answers are computed ...

item.title: Reflection Is Not Always Worth It: Budgeted Reflection Allocation for Recommendation Agents
item.description: This work aims to make recommendation agents more efficient by reducing unnecessary LLM reflection while preserving full-catalog ranking and inference reranking. Since BRAVE changes only how training-time reflection is allocated, it does not introduce new user data requirements or additional LLM exposure beyond the base agent protocol. The main potential risk is that a poorly calibrated allocator may assign less reflection to users whose preferences are sparse, niche, or under-represented, which...

item.title: CLEAR: Legible and Steerable Recommendation via Grounded Natural-Language Interests
item.description: Modern recommenders keep learned preferences in representations people cannot inspect or change. We present CLEAR (Controllable and Legible End-to-end Architecture for Recommendation), an end-to-end system deployed at Meta and built around an editable natural-language interest layer. CLEAR makes a ranked subset of inferred interests readable and stores accepted additions and suppressions as authoritative preference state. Behavioral grounding maps each inferred interest back to supporting events...

item.title: User First Intelligence: Three Measurements of Search and AI-Answer Analytics (SEO and GEO/AEO), and a Knowledge-Graph Framework for Query Discovery Beyond Search Volume
item.description: People say what they want to know in many places besides a search box, and the tools that search and AI-answer optimization (SEO and GEO/AEO) rely on see only part of that demand, through models reported as counts. This paper reports three measurements of such instruments and a framework. On the area-code section of a large US telecom provider's site, two commercial analytics platforms differed on estimated monthly visits by 7.5x to 27.1x (8.6x to 29.9x worldwide); across twelve sections of the ...

item.title: LABEL: Literature Asymmetry between Efficacy and Limits in Drug Knowledge and Language Models
item.description: Every medication comes with two types of medical facts: indications, which describe what conditions the drug treats (benefits), and contraindications, which describe who must avoid it to prevent serious harm (safety limits). Although contraindications are critical for patient safety and FDA regulations require listing them as rigorously as indications, we find that contraindications are far less documented than indications in general prose. In this paper, we measure how often these texts contain...

item.title: Knowledge-Guided Local-to-Global Anomaly Learning for Longitudinal Medication Trajectories
item.description: Detecting suspicious deviations in longitudinal medication trajectories requires distinguishing knowledge-consistent treatment variations from anomalous changes and linking local deviations to account-level decisions. We propose a knowledge-guided local-to-global (L2G) anomaly learning framework that addresses both challenges. It constructs proxy supervision at three granularities: medication occurrences, treatment episodes, and contiguous visit segments. Knowledge-consistent medication and epis...

item.title: Keep it Simple! A Multiple-Choice Task can Benefit Generative Recommendation
item.description: Sequential recommendation has recently witnessed growing interest in generative retrieval. One of the most popular approaches is to autoregressively generate the semantic identifiers (SIDs) of items as recommendations. Existing efforts mainly rely on semantic alignment, sophisticated architectural designs, and extensive hyperparameter tuning. However, the conventional learning framework for generative models could have foundational limitations. Specifically, most generative models directly predi...

item.title: LMEG-Doc: Layout-Grounded Multi-View Evidence Graphs for Multimodal Long-Document Retrieval
item.description: Retrieving relevant evidence from multimodal long documents remains challenging, as supporting information is often distributed across different pages and modalities. Existing retrieval methods primarily rank document elements by their individual similarity to a question, often overlooking relationships among complementary evidence. Consequently, relevant figures and tables may receive low retrieval scores even when they contain essential information. To address this limitation, we introduce LME...

item.title: Label-Free Detection of Structural Bias in LLM-Based Recommender Systems via Randomized Paraphrasing: The Case of Verbosity
item.description: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as recommenders in e-commerce and conversational shopping systems, where they select a product from a set of retrieved candidates described in natural language. Their decisions should depend on relevance to the user query, but may also be influenced by surface-level properties of the descriptions, such as their length. Detecting such structural biases is difficult because relevance labels are rarely available. We propose a label-free framewo...

item.title: StreamEmbed: Real-Time Indexing from Pixels for Screenshot Retrieval
item.description: Screen history can serve as searchable visual memory for people and agents, but unlike an offline corpus, it must be encoded and indexed as each screenshot arrives. OCR-based indexing is fast but loses visual information; visual encoding takes over two seconds. Yet screens change incrementally: most pixels repeat within and across screenshots. This raises a question: do visual encoders need to recompute their representations from scratch for every new screenshot? We present StreamEmbed, a system...

item.title: Explanations that Transfer: Interpreting Medical Retrieval with Sparse AutoEncoders
item.description: Medical AI systems that answer users' queries rely on retrieving medical knowledge from large document collections. In this context, finetuning general models on medical datasets can improve retrieval relevance. Yet the dense embeddings underlying modern retrieval systems remain largely opaque, making it difficult to understand the mechanics behind their results. Moreover, adapting to a specific medical dataset risks losing transferability to new clinical corpora. In this work, we tackle these i...

item.title: MeReader: An Offline, Privacy-Preserving, Progress-Aware AI Assistant for Narrative eBook Reading
item.description: This paper introduces MeReader, a privacy-preserving, offline and progress-aware AI assistant designed to function as a contextual companion for narrative reading on consumer hardware. Unlike conventional Large Language Model (LLM)-based systems that process documents/books online in an all-texts-at-once type of way, thereby risking narrative spoilers, MeReader confines both retrieval and generation to the reader's distinct position in the text. The system integrates a hybrid retrieval architect...

item.title: RecMem: Recurrent Memory Compression for Long-Sequence Generative Recommendation
item.description: Generative recommendation benefits from long interaction histories, but the cost of processing them directly grows with history length. We propose RecMem, a recurrent memory compression framework guided by three desiderata: space invariance, semantic fidelity, and lifelong evolvability. RecMem compresses historical segments into a fixed set of memory slots using a bifurcated encoder-decoder with shared lower layers and slot-wise forget-gated updates. Recommendation supervision trains the memory ...

item.title: RACE: Ranking-Uncertainty Aware Capacity-Adaptive Customization for Efficient Sequential Recommendation
item.description: Efficient sequential recommendation has emerged as a promising paradigm for providing real-time personalized service. To deploy models under resource-constrained environment, model compression becomes a necessity, yet existing methods typically apply uniform compression ratios, overlooking the heterogeneity in user intent complexity. This "one-size-fits-all" approach leads to a fundamental Capacity-Complexity Mismatch, where computational resources are either wasted on simple instances or insuff...

item.title: Who Counts as Exposed? Measurement Choices in an Open, Re-estimable Index of Occupational AI Exposure
item.description: Occupational AI exposure indices are used as inputs to economic analysis, workforce planning, and policy, and the choices built into them decide which workers are described as exposed. We build an open, re-estimable task-level index and vary its two main design decisions, context and calibration, to show how much the answer depends on them. For each of the 18,796 occupation--task pairs in \onet, seven open-weight reasoning models rate exposure under a common rubric. Each model rates with or with...

item.title: Towards High-Performance Multimodal Discovery: Evaluating Retrieval Efficacy and Operational Scalability in Digital Libraries
item.description: Large-scale digital repositories with million plus digitized volumes serve as vital engines for scientific and scholarly discovery. However, as collections grow, finding specific research or educational material remains a significant challenge. This difficulty is compounded by the multimodal nature of texts, that is, texts which combine dense narrative content with essential illustrative charts, annotated diagrams, and complex layouts. Historically, discovery has been supported by full-text sear...

item.title: Anonymous in Name Only: A Critical Review and a Reidentification Exercise on the European Commission's Anonymization Measures for Google Search Data under Article 6(11) of the DMA
item.description: In July 2026, the European Commission (EC) set out the anonymization measures Alphabet must implement to share Google Search data with competing search engines under Article 6(11) of the Digital Markets Act. As the first concrete illustration of how the EC operationalizes anonymization under the EU digital rulebook, this methodology could become a regulatory benchmark. In this paper, we show why it should not. We critically review the anonymization measures proposed by the EC, from the character...

item.title: From Tokens to Behaviors: Rethinking Generative Recommendation for User Trajectory Prediction
item.description: User behavior trajectory prediction (UBTP) aims to capture how a user&apos;s needs evolve over time by predicting the sequence of future interactions from that user&apos;s interaction history. Recent generative recommendation (GR) methods address this task through autoregressive generation of semantic IDs (SIDs). However, serial SID decoding couples token generation with behavior state transitions and requires multiple dependent steps per interaction. Discrete item feedback overlooks predictive uncertaint...

item.title: Evaluation of Music Version Retrieval Methods for Setlist Identification in Live Concerts
item.description: Automatic setlist identification aims to identify the songs performed in live concert recordings by matching noisy and variable-quality audio against a database of reference tracks. This task presents challenges beyond conventional music version identification, including substantial arrangement differences, background noise, and the need to process continuous recordings efficiently at large scale. In this work, we evaluate modern music version retrieval methods for setlist identification using t...

item.title: GA-HEL: A Knowledge-Driven Expert System for Open-Set, Granularity-Aware Hierarchical Event Linking in Social Media
item.description: Social-media event intelligence requires a system to determine whether a post belongs to a registered event space, identify the supported hierarchy path, and stop at the deepest level warranted by the evidence. We formulate this requirement as open-set hierarchical event linking over frozen Storyline--Episode--Atomic Event Cards. GA-HEL implements a three-stage, knowledge-driven expert-system funnel: open-set scope control limits candidate exposure before hierarchical reasoning, hierarchy-aware ...

item.title: HyperPage: Learned Page Layouts for Disk-Resident Graph Vector Indexes
item.description: Disk-resident graph indexes such as DiskANN store each vector with its graph edges as one record on SSD pages. A search needs the page of every record it expands, so its page reads depend on the page layout, that is, which records share a page. Search agents trained with reinforcement learning query one such index run after run, and every graph traversal can be logged with the records it expands. We therefore use the logs of a finished run to lay out the index for a declared memory budget, so la...

item.title: Bag of concepts can enhance other text representations for medical systematic review screening
item.description: The paper examines the choice of text representation for semi-automated systematic literature review (SLR) systems based on active learning. Motivated by the insufficient attention that the bag of concepts representation has received so far, the paper discusses the implementation and experimental evaluation of several variations thereof. The experimental study was performed on medical SLR case studies, with results reported for random forest classification, cluster initialization and uncertainty...

item.title: When Direction Matters: Diagnosing Relational Instruction Following in Dense Retrieval
item.description: Dense retrievers increasingly claim the ability to condition retrieval on natural-language relevance criteria beyond a short query. We identify a specific weakness in this capability: the evaluated models perform well when lexical or attribute cues distinguish the target, but become much less reliable when relevance depends on a directional relation over the same entities. We introduce SwitchIR, a controlled diagnostic that contrasts Constraint Shift and Explicit Filtering with Relational Flip, ...

item.title: SimRec: Learning to Search, Ask, and Recommend from Simulated Interaction
item.description: LLM-based recommendation agents can search catalogs, inspect products, ask users, and revise rejected recommendations. However, these behaviors are often governed by hand-designed workflows, while existing training methods optimize isolated components such as query rewriting or list ranking rather than the interaction policy as a whole. We present SimRec, a reinforcement learning framework that trains the full interaction policy of a tool-integrated recommendation agent. SimRec introduces two co...

item.title: Predicting the Needle in a Petabyte Scale Haystack: Open-Vocabulary Event Anticipation in Satellite Imagery
item.description: Satellite constellations now image the Earth daily, capturing the lifecycle of events from deforestation to urban construction. Anticipating these events before completion enables timely intervention, yet existing systems cannot jointly identify where a change occurs, what it will become, and when it will finish across an open vocabulary. Building such a model requires diverse event data, but events are like needles in a haystack, making manual annotation at global scale infeasible. We address t...

item.title: SignalAudit-QD: A Reproducible Audit Resource for External Signals in AI-Query Forecasting
item.description: SignalAudit-QD is a reproducible audit resource for testing whether a dated public signal adds information beyond query history in a fixed 20-term U.S. AI panel. It aligns two archived Google Trends extractions with eight USPTO AI-patent publication streams and releases origin-indexed predictions, paired losses, provenance, executable tests, and tamper-evident run manifests. Both inputs are retrospective reconstructions obtained after the modeled 2020--2023 origins; the task is therefore a pseud...

item.title: Sheaf-Inspired Structured Scoring Extensions of LightGCN for Collaborative Filtering
item.description: Graph-based collaborative filtering learns user and item representations by propagating embeddings over a user--item interaction graph. We investigate a modular, sheaf-inspired scoring extension placed on top of a three-layer LightGCN backbone. The motivation comes from cellular sheaves, where local vector spaces are related by linear restriction maps; here, this idea motivates structured, pair-dependent transformations of user and item embeddings rather than a change to graph propagation. We co...

item.title: Similar but Not Redundant: Embedding-Gated Refinement for High-Granularity Topic Models
item.description: High-granularity topic modelling extracts hundreds of niche topics from a corpus, yet this regime is rarely studied and is more commonly framed as a failure mode: &amp;quot;over-clustering,&amp;quot; in which coherent themes fragment into redundant subtopics. We argue that this framing conflates genuine redundancy with topics that are semantically similar but meaningfully distinct, and that the central challenge in high-granularity modelling is separating the two. Recent post-hoc refinement methods address topic ...

item.title: KuaiRecV2: Benchmarking Large-Scale Continual Learning for Diversified and Multi-task Recommendation
item.description: Recommender systems, which retrieve items of interest to users based on their interaction histories, have recently witnessed several key technological advancements, benefiting from the semantic representation space and model-data scaling. Nevertheless, practitioners and researchers have frequently encountered critical inconsistencies between simple offline evaluations and complex online results, and this gap still exists in the era of large models. In this work, we address several key factors th...

item.title: Active Learning of Approximate LLM Ranking for Energy-Efficient Retrieval of Long Queries
item.description: Search engines and Large Language Models (LLMs) offer complementary strengths for document retrieval: lexical retrievers which rely on keyword matching are fast and energy-efficient, whereas LLMs capture semantic meaning and excel at interpreting long, context-rich queries. However, this comes at a cost that is computationally and energetically prohibitive. We propose the LLM Active Approximation Model (LAAM), a hybrid retrieval framework that introduces a lightweight learned predictor which ser...

item.title: RMIT-ADM+S at TREC RAG 2026: Research Agents, Retriever Ablations, and Open-Weight Replication
item.description: We describe the RMIT-ADM+S team&amp;apos;s participation in the TREC 2026 Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) track using the ClimbMix corpus. We submitted seven research-agent runs using proprietary OpenAI and open-weight models, exploring different retrieval strategies, writer models, and agent workflows. Pre-submission ablations identified writer selection and adjacent-chunk expansion as the main factors affecting answer quality. In the official NIST evaluation, six of seven runs exceeded the track m...

item.title: AntEmbed: Dual-Mode Multimodal Embedding Model for Efficient and Fine-Grained Retrieval
item.description: Discriminative embeddings encode original multimodal inputs efficiently but struggle with fine-grained semantics. Generative embeddings use reasoning to capture query intent and relevance evidence, but incur higher computational costs. We propose AntEmbed, a dual-mode multimodal embedding model that supports efficient retrieval and reasoning-enhanced fine-grained matching in a unified embedding space. First, we construct retrieval-oriented reasoning content that captures query intent and confusi...

item.title: ReSID: Rethinking Long-Tail Retrieval in Generative Recommendation through Item Reachability
item.description: Generative recommendation (GR) represents items with discrete Semantic IDs (SIDs) and casts retrieval as sequence generation. Under skewed interaction distributions and tight serving budgets, GR struggles to retrieve long-tail items. In this work, we are the first to study long-tail reachability across the complete pipeline of SID construction, decoding, and matching. We find that under equal code lengths, parallel SID construction consistently outperforms sequential SIDs on tail items. Moreover...

item.title: TriGen: A Generative Paradigm for Trigger-Induced Recommendation
item.description: Generative recommendation typically operates under the User-Induced Recommendation (UIR) setting, predicting target items by autoregressively generating semantic IDs as a passive continuation of long-term user history. However, this paradigm overlooks Trigger-Induced Recommendation (TIR), an essential industrial scenario where a user click triggers an immediate follow-up feed. In TIR, recommendations must dynamically align with the instant trigger intent without compromising historical preferenc...

item.title: CURATOR: Scalable Fine-grained Evidence Selection for Retrieval-Augmented Generation using Decision Models
item.description: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) provides entire retrieved passages to the LLM, even though only a handful of spans within them contain the evidence pertaining to the question. While precise selection of these spans can improve context utilization, identifying them in isolation is challenging. A span may appear irrelevant by itself, and deciding whether to retain it may require examining other retrieved information. One can evaluate each span&amp;apos;s candidacy with the full retrieved context, but ...

item.title: When Local Definitions Are Missing: Stable Errors in Language Models
item.description: Contracts, technical manuals, and online communities often give familiar words special meanings and define them in one place. A language model that reads a passage without that definition may use the usual meaning and give an answer that sounds right but is wrong. We study this with multiple-choice questions whose correct answers depend on a local definition. The questions come from a synthetic vocabulary, commercial contracts, Reddit community glossaries, and the documentation of a decentralize...

item.title: Calibrated Early Termination with Bounded Optimality Gaps for Constrained Vector Search
item.description: Vector search over learned embeddings is the retrieval layer of recommendation and retrieval-augmented generation, and many applications cap how many answer items one category may contribute. Graph indexes answer a query by best-first traversal, and where it stops determines its cost and whether its answer is exact. item.title: REWEAVE: Online Learning for Workload-Adaptive HNSW Indexes

item.description: Multilingual Text-Based Person Retrieval (TBPR) aims to retrieve individuals with texts in multiple languages.
